claim.quote: A profile-likelihood ratio analysis shows the data to be consistent with a background-only hypothesis, setting new limits on spin-independent WIMP-nucleon, spin-dependent WIMP-neutron, and spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross sections for WIMP masses above 9 GeV/c².

date.note: Announcement date: the collaboration and SURF released the SR1 result on 7 July 2022. The paper was posted to arXiv on 8 July 2022 and published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 041002 (2023).

key_value.note: Spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section, 90% CL, at a WIMP mass of 36 GeV/c², from 60 live days and a 5.5 t fiducial mass.
key_value.quote: The most stringent limit is set for spin-independent scattering at 36 GeV/c², rejecting cross sections above 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at the 90% confidence level.

summary.plain: In its first 60 days of running, LZ saw nothing that looked like dark matter. That absence was itself the result: it ruled out a wide range of possible dark matter particles more tightly than any experiment before it.
summary.technical: SR1: 60 live days, 5.5 t fiducial, 23 Dec 2021 - 11 May 2022. Data consistent with background only; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 9.2e-48 cm2 excluded at 90% CL at 36 GeV/c2, with limits also set on spin-dependent WIMP-neutron and WIMP-proton couplings above 9 GeV/c2.

title: First Dark Matter Search Results from the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment
why_it_matters: LZ's very first 60 days of data already set the world's tightest limit on heavy WIMP dark matter, showing that the detector worked as designed and closing off a large region of parameter space that earlier experiments could not reach.
